title: Agent gate: scoped term and mail tokens, chat attribution by socket
what:
src/agent/:
- token.rs:
  - At start, when the flags are given, mint a term token and a mail token (harnox::crypto::random_token).
  - Write each with write_atomic_0600 to --term-token-file / --mail-token-file, then verify owner and mode 0600; refuse to start otherwise.
  - --agent-url-file gets http://<bound>/.
  - All three are removed on clean exit and rotate every start. Off by default, so tests never touch HOME. No token is ever in argv or env (hub.md 10.4).
- authenticate(ctx, req, scope): the Bearer is compared in constant time (subtle) against that scope's token only. A master bearer or cookie on an agent path gets 404. A scoped token anywhere else stays the ordinary 401.
- attrib.rs, from the Peer extension:
  1. Find the /proc/net/tcp (and tcp6) row whose local address equals the peer and whose remote address equals the bound address; take its inode.
  2. Find the live door pid from registry.door_pids() whose /proc/<pid>/fd holds socket:[inode].
  3. Map the pid to the chat id.
  Door pids only, with no ancestor walk. Refused with 403 'term tools work in chats this Minerva opened': a bash or curl child of a door, subagent children, the TUI and workflow runs.
- POST /hub/term/a/whoami and /hub/mail/a/whoami -> {chat}.
- fake_eidolon/agent.rs: with FAKE_AGENT_CALL=<verb>:<json> the fake door process itself calls the perch from its own socket, and it can also spawn `sh -c curl` (the child case).
tests:
tests/agent.rs:
- the token files are 0600, rotate across restarts and are gone after SIGTERM; no flags means no files
- a master bearer on /hub/term/a/whoami gets 404; the term token on /hub/sessions gets 401; the mail token on term routes gets 401
- the fake door's whoami returns its chat id; a curl from the test process gets 403; the door's `sh -c curl` child gets 403
- 1000 attributions with 16 doors take under 1 s
live_check: fake perch on PORT=48112 with --term-token-file under the temp HOME: curl whoami from the shell gets 403; the fake door's call returns its id.
risk: This is a guard rail, not a boundary: a same-uid process can read the master token (hub.md:302). The token files persist on disk, and a crash leaves a stale, rotated one. A second perch with the flags under the same HOME overwrites the first one's files; only your main perch passes them.
